<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as bologna luncheon meat

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-bologna-luncheon-meat" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-bologna-luncheon-meat-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of bologna luncheon meat, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-bologna-luncheon-meat" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-bologna-luncheon-meat" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in bologna luncheon meat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in bologna luncheon meat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, bologna luncheon meat, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (3.35 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (8 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (0.84 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (4 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-bologna-luncheon-meat" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-bologna-luncheon-meat" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in bologna luncheon meat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in bologna luncheon meat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same bologna luncheon meat.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Bologna luncheon meat, canned (5 city composites) had lead higher at 70.3 µg/kg, against 10.3 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (bologna luncheon meat, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-bologna-luncheon-meat-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-bologna-luncheon-meat-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in bologna luncheon meat is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in bologna luncheon meat is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 4 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR 2012 reported inorganic arsenic at 6 µg/kg (mean) in bologna luncheon meat, as sold from all samples (4 sampling occasions, composites).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span
